title: Anarchists in the Tenant Movement #3 – the Southeast
content:
This is the third installment of our Anarchists in the Tenant Movement series. You can find the first installment here and the second here . The interview below was conducted with an organizer named Mario, involved in a tenant union in the US Southeast. We’ve concealed Mario’s specific location at his request.

Like our other series Anarchists in the Labor Movement , these interviews aim to capture insights and perspectives from anarchists who are active in tenant organizing. Some of those we speak to are organizing through established tenant unions, others are building new unions, while others still are launching initial campaigns without a formal union yet.

For Black Rose / Rosa Negra (BRRN), mass organizations like tenant unions play a central role in our strategy . It’s through these kinds of organizations that people create and apply their collective leverage against structures that dominate and exploit us, such as landlordism and private property. By engaging consistently in everyday campaigns members of mass organizations grow their collective confidence and power, enabling them to take on ever bigger fights and ultimately to challenge the very existence of these dominating structures.

title: Black Rose/Rosa Negra Bay Area Local Raises Thousands for MN15 Defense Fund
content:
On June 16th the federal government unsealed indictments targeting 15 organizers in Minnesota’s Twin Cities for their alleged involvement in anti-ICE organizing. On July 4th, the Bay Area Local of Black Rose/Rosa Negra held a party to raise money for these organizers’ legal defense fund. 







On July 4th, 2026 Black Rose/Rosa Negra’s Bay Area Local hoisted the red-and-black flag over Oakland’s 

Tamarack

 social center to party in solidarity with the 15 organizers—now known as the MN15—who were indicted by the federal government for allegedly organizing to stop ICE’s campaign of terror during operation ‘

Metro Surge

‘. Sharing food, stiff drinks, conversation, and dancing to tunes provided by local DJ collective 

Left of the Dial

, a couple hundred tenants, workers, students, movement elders, and comrades new and old raised over $2,000 for the MN15’s 

legal defense fund.







 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

View this post on Instagram

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

A post shared by @blackrosebayarea







Part way through the night the music stopped to allow for two of the indicted organizers to call in and share words of encouragement. The call was piped through the social center’s PA system for all partygoers to hear. These indictments were a “naked attempt by the federal government to intimidate popular forms of resistance and by isolating its revolutionary wing”,
